title: Emotional Burnout
what_it_looks_like: Emotional burnout is often the result of prolonged stress. You might feel emotionally overwhelmed, depleted, or unable to cope with even small challenges. Relationships may suffer because you feel too drained to invest emotionally.
signs: Feeling detached or disconnected from loved ones
Difficulty managing emotions like anger or sadness
Feeling empty or emotionally numb
Overreacting to minor issues
healing_steps: Emotional burnout requires nurturing your emotional resilience and learning to regulate your nervous system.

title: Physical Burnout
what_it_looks_like: Physical burnout occurs when your body has been pushed beyond its limits, often from lack of rest, poor diet, or chronic illness. You might feel constantly fatigued, even after sleep, and experience persistent aches, pains, or other physical symptoms.
signs: Constant fatigue, regardless of rest
Muscle aches, headaches, or chronic pain
Weak immune system or frequent illnesses
Difficulty concentrating or completing daily tasks
healing_steps: Physical burnout is your body's way of asking for deep rest and restoration.

title: Mental Burnout
what_it_looks_like: Mental burnout stems from overwhelming cognitive demands, like constant multitasking or problem-solving. You might feel mentally drained, have trouble focusing, or struggle to remember things. Mental exhaustion can make it difficult to be productive or think creatively.
signs: Brain fog or forgetfulness
Struggling to concentrate or make decisions
Feeling mentally fried or overwhelmed
Difficulty engaging with tasks you once enjoyed
healing_steps: Mental burnout can benefit from brain retraining and neuroplasticity techniques.

title: Social Burnout
what_it_looks_like: Social burnout occurs when you feel overwhelmed or drained by social interactions. This type of burnout is common in people who feel obligated to care for others or maintain relationships, leading to feelings of resentment or isolation.
signs: Irritability or frustration in social situations
Avoiding social events or gatherings
Feeling like you have nothing to give emotionally to others
Resentment toward those who need your help or support
healing_steps: Setting healthy boundaries and learning to balance social connections with self-care is key.

title: Purpose-Driven Burnout
what_it_looks_like: Purpose-driven burnout happens when you are deeply passionate about your work but feel unfulfilled or stuck. You may start to question the meaning of what you are doing, feel underappreciated, or even consider abandoning your goals.
signs: Feeling like your work or passion no longer brings joy
Struggling with a sense of hopelessness or dissatisfaction
Questioning your purpose or life path
Feeling like no matter how hard you work, it is never enough
healing_steps: Reconnecting with your deeper purpose and learning to manage stress around your goals can reignite your passion.
